newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Sept 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Sept 25.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- REBEL NAMES ON MISSION TO END CITY FRAUD

A group of Lloyd's of London Names are to launch a new foundation in London aimed at ending City fraud for good. At a meeting tomorrow the United Names Organisation will set up a "Foundation for the Rights of Man". The organisation is aiming to recruit from the 1,850 Lloyd's members who have turned down the insurance market's 3.2 billion stg settlement offer and to secure full restitution for members.
-- WIMPEY DEAL BRINGS 1,400 JOB LOSSES AT TARMAC
The construction and building materials group, Tarmac, has revealed that it has cut 1,000 jobs in the wake of is asset swap with Wimpey and plans 400 more redundancies by the end of the year.
-- JERSEY OFFERS LEGAL HAVEN FOR ACCOUNTANTS

Jersey's parliament has approved legislation to allow limited-liability partnerships that would defend auditors from litigation, thus clearing the way for Britain's major accountancy firms to move their headquarters offshore to protect members. The new law was introduced at the behest of two of the Big Six accountancy firms, Price Waterhouse and Ernst and Young.
THE TIMES
-- GEORGE WALKER'S SIX MILLION STG PUTS BRENT WALKER IN PERIL

Leisure group Brent Walker is facing the threat of collapse after a judge in France granted an award for more than six million stg in favour of the company's founder George Walker. Brent Walker appealed against the decision. The court outcome poses a threat to the planned disposal of the Pubmaster pubs chain, which is on the market for 200 million stg and the sale of betting chain William Hill.
-- UK AND U.S. INTEREST RATES STAY ON HOLD

Following the meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee the US Federal Reserve has left American interest rates unchanged at 5.25 per cent. A poll conducted by Reuters found that 31 of 55 economists expected the Fed to raise rates. The Dow Jones industrial average was boosted by 30 points by the news, but then the key index then settled back for only modest gains. Before the meeting President Clinton told reporters that he was very pleased that America was enjoying strong growth with no sign of inflation.
-- RANK PAYS 95 MILLION STG FOR TOM COBLEIGH

The Rank Organisation is to pay 95.5 million stg for pub group Tom Cobleigh. Rank intends to accelerate the growth of the chain by introducing pub restaurants into its cinema complexes and multi-leisure centres. Rank are attracted to Tom Cobleigh's high proportion of food sales, which make up half total revenues in its newer and larger pubs. The four executive directors of Tom Cobleigh are set to become millionaires.
THE GUARDIAN
-- AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL FOR SALE

According to unions and construction firms, the Government is looking into the possibility of rushing through the privatisation of Britain's air traffic control service due to the increasing problems in modernising the system through its Private Finance Initiative. The Treasury and Department of Transport are planning to either sell off the service or offer it on franchise in a move which could raise between 600 million stg and one billion stg for the Treasury ahead of the election.
-- CLARKE FILLIP AS FIGURES LOOK BRIGHT

Latest figures show that the British economy is more buoyant than authorities had estimated. The Government has welcomed a surprise 0.5 billion stg surplus on the balance of payments in the second quarter, and latest estimates of GDP growth brought Chancellor Kenneth Clarke one step closer to this year's 2.5 per cent target. City analysts warned that the unexpectedly good figures mean that the Chancellor's resistance to raising the base rates from 5.75 per cent was under renewed pressure.
-- ROGUE TRADER COST UBS 500,000 STG

UBS, the securities group, nearly lost half a million stg through the activities of Mark Larkin, a rogue trader, who defied orders on secret dealings and hid his trades. The bank lost a further 8.9 million stg on legitimate deals that had been misrecorded to hide losses. Action by regulators against Mr Larkin and one of his subordinates shows up a number of incidents of wrong-doing at UBS in the early 1990s.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- WATCHDOG UNCOVERS WATER PROFITS MISUSE

Water industry regulator Ian Byatt has revealed evidence showing how the ten privatised water companies have used their profits to subsidise hundreds of million of stg of activities though a system of unregulated businesses. Six months of investigations by independent inspectors appointed by the industry watchdog, Ofwat, unveiled the extend of the conflicts of interest and cross-subsidies.
-- TELEWEST REJECTS GSB CHANNELS

The UK's largest cable operator Telewest is refusing to carry seven new television channels backed by BSkyB and Granada until it has canvassed its subscribers about whether they are willing to pay for the services. The move will step up the conflict between BSkyB and the UK's cable operators. According to Telewest, the decision was prompted by its concern that subscribers would be unwilling go pay an extra one pound stg a month for their basic cable television package.
-- IOD WARNING AGAINST TAX CUTS

The Institute of Directors have issued a warning to the Government not to cut taxes in November's Budget. They urged Chancellor Kenneth Clarke to correct an "alarming" deterioration in public finances. In its pre-budget submission, written by the former senior Treasury economic advisor Stephen Davies, the IOD called for seven billion stg to be removed from Government revenues and that five billion stg could come from public spending cuts and a further two billion stg from the Treasury's reserves.
